messages:
evan_runtime: noticing intermittent hangs on 8-node TP runs since yesterday deploy. looks like wall-clock stalls that resolve after 30-90s. any quick ideas? :thinking:

maya_infra: ugh. saw something similar on staging earlier. timeline shows a step-shaped increase in all-reduce wait time across ranks.

jia_ml: can you paste the perf trace? curious if kernel selection changed or if kv cache shards are misaligned.

evan_runtime: here's the short trace from one run (trimmed):
```
2024-06-02T14:12:11Z rank0 enter forward_layer 42
2024-06-02T14:12:12Z rank0 launch matmul_kernel_q8
2024-06-02T14:12:12Z rank0 enqueue allreduce size=48MB
2024-06-02T14:12:12Z rank1 enqueue allreduce size=48MB
2024-06-02T14:12:12Z rank2 wait allreduce completion +62.1s <-- stall
2024-06-02T14:12:12Z rank3 wait allreduce completion +62.3s
```

evan_runtime: also attached kvcache stats: high shard variance, some ranks showing 20% more insert misses.

perf-bot: profile upload: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/1719993333 (contains nvprof, custom timeline) :robot_face:

maya_infra: interesting: kernel selector log shows a sudden fallback to a non-fused matmul on ranks 2-3 for long sequences. could be a codepath mismatch causing extra memcopies before allreduce.

jia_ml: that matches the kvcache observation — when kernels change we sometimes change the KvBuffer layout (alignment/padding). If padding differs by rank, kv indices shift and shards get different sizes.

sam_sre: could that lead to rank desync? i thought RPC checks would catch header mismatches.

evan_runtime: RPC sees messages but allreduce op sizes are identical on enqueue. it's the timing that's diverging — some ranks spend extra time in pre-allreduce memcpy. leads to an allreduce window starve then timeout.

jia_ml: quick repro idea: force uniform kernel by setting KERNEL_PREFER=fast_fused for all ranks and rerun a 8-node ephemeral job. see if stalls disappear.

maya_infra: will run now on the repro cluster (staging-gpu-8). also doing a run with KV_DEBUG=1 to print shard sizes.

[7m later]

maya_infra: run1 with forced fused kernels: no hang, median allreduce latency down from 2.1s to 0.12s. KV shard skew gone.

evan_runtime: so kernel selection divergence is the trigger. root causes: selector heuristics + sequence-length conditional that wasn't deterministic across nodes.

jia_ml: probable codepath: when seq_len > 1024 we pick kernel-v2 which inserts a 64-byte pad for alignment. due to different micro-batches, some ranks crossed threshold earlier.

sam_sre: action items: 1) short-term: pin kernel selector to fused across all TP nodes for the next deploy 2) add a deterministic kernel selection barrier in rendezvous (all ranks broadcast chosen kernel) 3) add KV shard checksum to detect layout desync earlier.

evan_runtime: +1. also add a perf alert when allreduce tail latency has >10x variance across ranks for 3 consecutive steps.

jia_ml: I'll open a PR to: a) make selector deterministic (broadcast choice) b) emit a kernel_id in the preflight metadata c) add a new kvcache evict metric for shard-size-variance.

maya_infra: running long soak with pinned kernels and KV_DEBUG. will post logs if anything pops.

perf-bot: regression check: compares last 5 successful runs vs current — flagging a 13% p50 increase in forward step on one build (suspect commit 3a2ef9 changed kernel thresholds).

evan_runtime: good find. tagging commit 3a2ef9 in the triage. jia, can you link the PR to revert/adjust thresholds?

jia_ml: will do. plan: revert threshold change, land deterministic broadcast, and add small unit test that runs selector determinism across simulated rank seeds.

sam_sre: i'll add a temporary watchdog that fails fast (and captures traces) instead of letting jobs sit for minutes. we should fail loudly for interp-hangs.

evan_runtime: sounds good. thanks all. please post PR and short run logs here when ready. :thumbsup:
